subject: POC success criteria and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jeong <alex.jeong@vertexai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC success criteria and mitigation plan

Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight plan for the 4‑week pilot so we can align on success metrics and surface risks early. Please scan and let me know edits.

Summary of call
- Goal: Validate Redwood can serve VertexAI’s multi-tenant embedding/semantic search workload at 200 qps with 99th-percentile latency < 150ms for 512-token queries.
- Primary constraints: data residency for search logs, integration with Vertex’s SSO, and ability to ingest ~1.2B vectors for cold-start evaluation.

Proposed pilot (weeks) and ownership
1) Week 0 (prep, 1 week): onboarding, infra checklist, test data subset (owner: Aditya).
2) Week 1–2 (integration): SSO + ingestion + baseline runs (owner: Marissa).
3) Week 3 (scale & quality): load run to 200 qps, quality evals against Vertex test set (owner: Stephanie).
4) Week 4 (wrap): final report, regen plan, and decision meeting (owners: Stephanie + Vertex PM).

Success criteria (pass/fail) — needs Vertex sign-off
- Latency: p99 < 150ms for 512-token queries (peak 200 qps)
- Throughput: sustained 200 qps over 10 min with <2% error rate
- Relevance: embedding-based recall >= 0.78 on Vertex evaluation set
- Security: SOC2 evidence reviewed; no open critical compliance items

Known risks & immediate mitigations
- Integration: SSO certificate exchange may require cert rotation window — Mitigation: schedule certificate handover day 0 and provide a fallback test identity (owner: Aditya).
- Cold-start ingestion: 1.2B vectors is heavy for initial run — Mitigation: staggered shard upload + prefix cache warmup (owner: Marissa).
- Blocking bug potential: on-prem connector may require kernel-level library that Vertex infra restricts — escalation path documented below.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Summary_2026.pdf (summary), sample PoC schedule (poc-schedule.xlsx stub coming).

Next steps (please confirm by EOD)
- Alex: confirm stakeholders and a preferred pilot start week (options: Mar 8 / Mar 15).
- Vertex: share SOC2 questionnaire (if you prefer, send initial answers).
- Redwood: we’ll prepare a DocuSign MOA for the pilot terms once you confirm start date.

Thanks — Steph

--

Thanks, Stephanie — helpful outline. A couple of items and a note on timelines:

- The 1.2B vector number is for full index; for pilot we want a representative shard of ~200M vectors. Can Redwood confirm expected ingest time for 200M?
- Security: I’m attaching the SOC2 questionnaire Vertex uses (vertexai-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx). Our security lead Heather will review Redwood_Security_Summary_2026 and follow up with questions.

Timeline
- Preferred start: Mar 15 to sync with our infra maintenance window.

Questions that may affect scope
- Does Redwood require any elevated network ports for the on-prem connector? We have strict egress rules.

I’ll loop Heather on answers. We can do Mar 15 start if we get confirmation on ports and a short MOA.

Regards,
Alex

Date: 2027-03-02T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria and mitigation plan

Looping in notes from infra triage this morning. Two potential blockers surfaced that we should flag in the risk register:

1) On‑prem connector kernel dependency: the connector uses a system-level library (libfastivm.so v2.x) that requires GLIBC > 2.29. Vertex infra images are pinned to 2.27. If Vertex cannot update, connector will fail to load. Mitigation options:
  - Option A (preferred): run connector in a small dedicated VM with compatible distro (we can provide an AMI/container).
  - Option B: use our hosted Dedicated pool and route traffic via secure peering for the pilot (adds network config but avoids on‑prem install).

2) Ingestion throughput estimate: our benchmarks show ~6 hours to ingest 200M vectors with the current shard/parallelism settings (assuming 8 workers). We can reduce to ~3 hours with an additional node or temporary burst capacity (cost + infra ask).

Short asks
- Stephanie: confirm whether Vertex will allow a dedicated VM OR if they prefer us to use Dedicated pool for the pilot.
- Alex: confirm the 200M shard size and availability of an SSO test account so we can validate auth flows before the start date.

I’ll update the risk column in the shared sheet after you confirm.

Aditya

Thanks Aditya — adding owners and escalation path.

Updated owners & escalation
- Integration / SSO certs: Aditya (owner). If Aditya cannot proceed due to cert exchange delays, escalate to Diego Fernandez (Infra Lead).
- On‑prem kernel incompatibility: Marissa (owner for workaround plan). Escalation -> Diego for approvals to run a dedicated VM or approve peering into Dedicated pool.
- Ingestion throughput: Aditya + Marissa to run a fast-path ingest (burst nodes) if initial ingest estimate is >4 hours. Escalation -> Stephanie to approve temporary budget for burst capacity.

I’ve added a short mitigation plan to the shared folder (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_POC-vertexai). I also created a simple risk table in the shared sheet.

Next internal step: Diego, can you confirm whether Redwood can provision a hardened VM image for Vertex by Mar 12? If yes, we can proceed with Mar 15 start.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: POC success criteria and mitigation plan

Marissa — we can provision a hardened VM image with GLIBC 2.31 and the connector preinstalled. Timeline: image ready by Mar 11 if infra approvals go through today. Two notes:

1) Networking: Vertex will need to open TCP 443 for peered endpoint traffic or accept our VM in their VPC with a private peering setup. Security review required on their side.
2) Limited support window: infra can support the VM and perform installs during business hours only; emergency patches carry an SLA and cost.

If Vertex cannot accept VM peering, we recommend using our Dedicated pool for the pilot. I’ll prepare the AMI and a short runbook for Aditya.

Diego

Subject: POC plan: final timeline, MOA, and risk register link

Alex — thanks for the quick replies. Based on infra confirmation from Diego, here’s the final plan and concrete next steps for a Mar 15 start.

Final pilot plan (Mar 15 — Apr 11) - Week 0 (Mar 15–Mar 19): VM exchange + SSO test account + ingest small shard (10M)
- Week 1 (Mar 22–Mar 26): Full ingestion for 200M shard (target: <4h using burst nodes)
- Week 2 (Mar 29–Apr 2): Scale runs to 200 qps, quality evals and p99 collection
- Week 3 (Apr 5–Apr 11): Wrap, final report, and decision meeting

Acceptance criteria (finalized)
- p99 latency < 150ms at 200 qps
- Ingest of 200M vectors in <4 hours (or documented mitigation if not met)
- Recall >= 0.78 on Vertex eval set
- No open critical security items after Heather’s SOC2 review

Escalation path (if a blocking issue occurs)
1) On-call SE (Aditya) — immediate triage
2) Infra lead (Diego) — if kernel/VM or peering issues
3) Steph (AE) — commercial implications and decisions (credits / Dedicated pool fallback)

Attachments & links
- PO C schedule attached: poc-schedule.xlsx (stub)
- MOA to sign: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABCDEF-2027
- Risk register & trackers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_POC-vertexai

Please confirm:
1) Vertex: Mar 15 start ok?
2) Heather: can you confirm you’ll deliver SOC2 feedback by Mar 9?

If all good, I’ll send the MOA for signature and we’ll kick off image provisioning this week.

Thanks — Steph
